verdict.rationale: Dagster defines assets, schedules, sensors, and declarative automation conditions in Python code or `defs.yaml` component files. That makes automations versionable and reviewable through ordinary source control, and a community comment credits Dagster with having "figured out how to do development branches." However, no evidence documents a first-party versioning, review, or rollback workflow; these capabilities are implied by code-as-definition rather than shown. Missing for 10: documented branch or preview deployments for reviewing changes, an explicit rollback mechanism for deployed code locations, in-product version history of automations, and hands-on corroboration.
